title: Fury
verdict_short: Yes. Goes down with his tank, shredded by grenades in a last stand.
how: In April 1945 Wardaddy's immobilized Sherman, 'Fury', makes a suicidal last stand at a crossroads against a Waffen-SS battalion. As ammo runs out he is hit by a German sniper, then, bleeding out inside the turret, orders Norman to escape through the floor hatch. SS troops drop stick grenades into the tank and the blasts kill him. The next morning Norman climbs back in and covers his corpse with his jacket before US reinforcements find him.
notes: He is the only member of the crew besides Norman who survives long enough to make the final choice; the rest of the crew die one by one in the same battle.

title: The Audition
verdict_short: No. He just steals the part from De Niro and DiCaprio.
how: A 16-minute promotional short for a Macau casino. Robert De Niro and Leonardo DiCaprio each pitch Martin Scorsese on why they should star in his next picture, only for Scorsese to reveal he has already cast Brad Pitt, who strolls in playing a smug version of himself. Nobody dies; the joke is the two stunned actors congratulating each other.
notes: Short film; reportedly the most expensive short ever made.

title: By the Sea
verdict_short: No. Finishes his novel and drives off with his wife.
how: Roland, a blocked American writer, spends a 1970s French seaside holiday drinking while his wife Vanessa (Angelina Jolie) grieves. The pair spy on newlyweds through a hole in the wall, Vanessa tries to seduce the young husband, and Roland punches him. The marriage's wound turns out to be Vanessa's miscarriages and infertility. They reconcile, Roland finishes his book about her, and they leave the hotel together, alive and slightly more hopeful.
notes: Written and directed by his then-wife Angelina Jolie; their last film together.

title: The Big Short
verdict_short: No. Cashes out and goes back to growing seeds in retirement.
how: Ben Rickert, a paranoid retired trader, helps two young investors (Charlie and Jamie) get the swaps that let them bet against the housing market. When the crash finally hits he sells their positions from a pub in England, scolding them for celebrating an economy's collapse. The epilogue notes he simply returned to his quiet retirement, alive and grumpy.
notes: Character is based on real trader Ben Hockett. Pitt also produced the film.

title: Hitting the Apex
verdict_short: No.
how: Documentary narration.

title: Voyage of Time
verdict_short: No.
how: Documentary narration.

title: Allied
verdict_short: No. He lives; his wife shoots herself on the runway.
how: Canadian intelligence officer Max Vatan marries French Resistance fighter Marianne after their Casablanca assassination mission, then learns she may be a German spy. Ordered to execute her if the 'blue dye' test proves it, Max instead kills her handlers and tries to fly her out. As military police close in on the airfield, Marianne tells Max she loves him, asks him to care for their daughter, and shoots herself. Max survives and raises Anna on a ranch in Medicine Hat, Alberta.

title: War Machine
verdict_short: No. Fired by the President after a Rolling Stone exposé.
how: McMahon, a swaggering four-star general (a thinly veiled Stanley McChrystal), arrives in Afghanistan in 2009 to 'win' the war and pushes for a 40,000-troop surge. He leaks his assessment, mouths off about the President, and lets a Rolling Stone reporter embed with his staff. The resulting article exposes his contempt for civilian leadership and he is summoned to Washington and relieved of command, quietly lining up a consultant gig on the way out. A new general is appointed to keep the war going.
notes: Netflix release. Satire based on Michael Hastings' book The Operators.

title: The Jim Jefferies Show
verdict_short: No. He just forecasts the end of the world.
how: Pitt turned up in the Comedy Central show's June 2017 premiere as a deadpan, tan-suited weatherman standing in front of a glowing red map after the U.S. pulled out of the Paris climate accord ('things are going to be getting warmer in this area here'). He returned several times across 2017 and 2018 as the show's unofficial, increasingly depressed weatherman. Nobody dies, but the planet is not doing great.
notes: Seven episodes, 2017 to 2018. Pitt reportedly asked to be on the show and was paid SAG scale.

title: Deadpool 2
verdict_short: Yes. Electrocuted on power lines, visible for about one second.
how: The invisible mutant Vanisher joins Deadpool's new X-Force team for a parachute drop onto a prison convoy. High winds scatter the team and kill them one by one; Vanisher is blown into high-voltage power lines and electrocuted, his face flickering into view for a split second to reveal it was Brad Pitt all along. Only Deadpool and Domino survive the jump.
notes: Uncredited surprise cameo; Pitt shot it in about two hours for scale. The same footage appears in the PG-13 recut Once Upon a Deadpool (2018). Deadpool's time-travel fix at the end saves Peter but not Vanisher.

title: Once Upon a Deadpool
verdict_short: Yes. Same power-line death, now PG-13.
how: Recut of Deadpool 2.
notes: Duplicate.

title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
verdict_short: No. Stabbed in the hip, but he beats the Manson Family to death and rides off in an ambulance.
how: On August 8, 1969, Cliff, tripping on an acid-dipped cigarette, is walking Brandy the pit bull when three Manson Family members break into Rick Dalton's house instead of Sharon Tate's. Cliff sics Brandy on Tex, stomps him to death, and after Katie stabs him in the hip he smashes her face in with a can of dog food and anything else within reach; Rick torches the third intruder with a flamethrower. Cliff is loaded into an ambulance alive, joking with Rick, while Rick gets invited up to Sharon Tate's house for a drink.
notes: Won Pitt the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

title: Ad Astra
verdict_short: No. Nukes his dad's space station and rides the shockwave home to Earth.
how: Roy travels to Neptune to stop the antimatter surges from his father's lost Lima Project station. He finds his father Clifford (Tommy Lee Jones) alive and unrepentant after killing his mutinous crew, plants a nuclear charge, and tries to bring him home. Clifford instead pushes off into space and asks to be let go; Roy releases the tether and watches him drift away. Roy uses the blast to slingshot back to Earth, where he lands safely and reconnects with his estranged wife.
notes: His father dies; Roy survives everything, including a Moon pirate chase and a rabid space baboon.

title: Saturday Night Live
verdict_short: No. Takes off the wig and thanks the real Fauci.
how: In the April 25, 2020 remote cold open, Pitt plays Dr. Fauci calmly 'translating' clips of the President's coronavirus statements, facepalming at the disinfectant and 'hit the body with light' ideas. At the end he removes the gray wig and glasses and, as himself, thanks Fauci and frontline workers. Nobody dies.
notes: Earned Pitt an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series.

title: The Lost City
verdict_short: No. But he's shot in the head and looks very dead until the mid-credits scene.
how: Jack Trainer, a glorious-haired ex-Navy SEAL, storms Fairfax's jungle compound and rescues Loretta (Sandra Bullock) in a one-man action sequence. During the escape he is shot in the head by a mercenary in front of a horrified Alan (Channing Tatum), and the movie treats him as dead for the rest of the runtime. In a mid-credits scene Loretta and Alan spot him alive at a meditation class; he shrugs that only 10% of his brain was in use anyway.
notes: Extended cameo of about 15 minutes. Apparent death around the end of act one; revealed alive mid-credits.

title: Bullet Train
verdict_short: No. Everyone else dies; his bad luck keeps him alive.
how: Anxious assassin Ladybug boards a Tokyo-to-Kyoto bullet train to grab a briefcase and instead gets tangled with Lemon, Tangerine, the Prince, the Hornet, and eventually the White Death. In the derailed wreckage the White Death shoots Ladybug with Ladybug's own gun, which the Prince had rigged to backfire, blowing off the villain's head. Ladybug limps out of the ruins into Maria's (Sandra Bullock) car, alive and complaining.
notes: Nearly everyone else on the train dies.

title: Babylon
verdict_short: Yes. Shoots himself in a hotel room once the talkies leave him behind.
how: Silent-era megastar Jack Conrad can't survive the transition to sound; audiences laugh at his voice and he's shoved into ensemble parts. In 1932, after his friend George Munn takes his own life, Jack confronts gossip columnist Elinor St. John, who tells him his star has faded but the films will make him immortal. He runs into Fay at a hotel party, learns she's leaving for Europe, returns to his room, and shoots himself; the gunshot is heard from the hallway.
notes: Death comes roughly two hours into the three-hour film, before the Manny and Nellie finale.

title: Dave
verdict_short: No. Takes a crossbow bolt to the chest but gives a thumbs-up to the paramedics.
how: After popping into Lil Dicky's 'Mr. McAdams' music video, Pitt shows up at Dave's house wanting a music mentor and ends up recording in his studio, only for obsessed fan Bella to take them (and GaTa) hostage at gunpoint. At the peak of the standoff Bella shoots Brad in the chest with a tour-branded arrow from Dave's prop crossbow. Bleeding out, he dispenses one last piece of wisdom ('Until you love yourself, you can never love another'); as paramedics rush in his hand rises in a thumbs-up, signalling he'll live.
notes: Aired May 31, 2023 on FXX. Outcome kept slightly ambiguous, but the creators and the thumbs-up confirm he survives.

title: IF
verdict_short: No. He's an invisible imaginary friend; you never see or hear him.
how: Keith is an invisible, silent imaginary friend that characters keep tripping over throughout John Krasinski's film. Pitt has no lines and no on-screen presence; his credit only appears at the end as a wink at his invisible Vanisher cameo in Deadpool 2 (also with Ryan Reynolds). No death, no body, no character arc.
notes: Credited voice cameo with zero audible dialogue.

title: Wolfs
verdict_short: No. Cuts to black as the diner shootout starts.
how: Two rival lone-wolf fixers (Pitt and George Clooney) are hired to clean up the same hotel-room 'corpse', which turns out to be a very alive kid full of drugs. After a night dodging Albanian mobsters and returning the stolen product, both are ordered to kill the Kid but choose not to. In the final scene hitmen surround them at a Brighton Beach diner; they agree to finally tell each other their names if they survive, start shooting, and the film cuts to black.
notes: Open-ended, but no death shown. Apple TV+ release; a planned sequel was cancelled.

title: F1
verdict_short: No. Wins Abu Dhabi and drives off to the next race.
how: Aging journeyman Sonny Hayes returns to Formula One with the failing APXGP team thirty years after a near-fatal 1993 crash. He walks away from more crashes (Silverstone, a fiery Las Vegas pileup that briefly gets him fired, a minor Abu Dhabi shunt) while hiding that his old injuries make him medically unfit to race. In the Abu Dhabi finale he holds off Lewis Hamilton, takes his first F1 win, saves the team, and is last seen heading off to race in Baja.
notes: Sonny's teammate Joshua Pearce also survives a serious crash.

title: Heart of the Beast
verdict_short: Yes. His failing heart gives out in the Alaskan wilderness; only the dog makes it to the road.
how: Retired Special Forces operator James Belmont suffers a heart attack while piloting a seaplane over Alaska and crashes, leaving him and his combat dog Odin 58 miles from the nearest road. Over a brutal week he breaks his arm in a river, nearly drowns, and is mauled defending Odin from a wolf pack, popping aspirin to keep his heart going. Near the end of the trek, wrecked by injuries and cardiac failure, he writes a letter for whoever finds Odin, gives the dog a final command to 'find the road', and dies alone in the wild. The film's opening flash-forward pays off as Odin emerges onto the road and is picked up by a young woman named Amber.
notes: Released September 25, 2026. Early recaps agree James dies and Odin lives; sources differ slightly on whether the wolf injuries or his heart is the proximate cause.

title: The Adventures of Cliff Booth
verdict_short: Not released yet.
how: Standalone sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. Set in 1977 Los Angeles, eight years after the Manson fight, with Cliff now working as a Hollywood studio fixer. No plot or ending has been released. The verdict lands here the week it opens.
notes: Formerly titled The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Cast includes Elizabeth Debicki, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Scott Caan and Peter Weller.
